raw.details:
Overview
Engineer an Intelligent Tech Stack Recommendation Engine!

About the Event:
Build an intelligent tech stack recommendation engine in the StackSense Challenge, a fully online systems-design competition at Synergy ‘26!

Participants must engineer an engine that takes project parameters such as scale, team size, budget and infrastructure constraints, and outputs an optimal combination of frontend, backend, database and hosting tools, backed by rigorous architectural reasoning.

Important Dates:

  • Problem Statement Release: 10 November 2026, 10:00 AM IST. The detailed problem statement, input/output specifications, sample scenarios and report template will be published here on Unstop.
  • Submission Deadline: 15 November 2026, 11:59 PM IST

Submission Instructions:
Submit a single Google Drive folder link on Unstop, with access set to “Anyone with the link can view”. The folder must contain:

  • Source Code: Includes a comprehensive README.md covering system architecture and local setup instructions.
  • Project Report (PDF): Details system design, input parameters collected, sample recommendation screenshots, and edge-case handling.

The exact folder structure and report template will be shared with the problem statement on 10 November.

Rules & Regulations:

  • Participation: Strictly individual; no team submissions or multi-member collaborations are allowed.
  • Third-Party Tools: Publicly available APIs, datasets, or open-source libraries are permitted, provided they are explicitly cited in the project report.
  • Originality: Submissions must be original and built during the challenge window. Plagiarized or pre-existing projects will result in immediate disqualification.
  • Late Submissions: Submissions after the deadline, or changes to the Drive folder after the deadline, will not be accepted.
  • Decisions: All decisions made by the organizing and judging panels are final.

Evaluation Criteria:

  • Recommendation Quality (35%): Correctness and architectural fit of the recommended stack against given project constraints. Engines will be tested on both public and hidden scenarios.
  • Input Design & Research (30%): Depth, relevance, and technical research behind the requirement-gathering process.
  • Reasoning & Explainability (20%): Quality of technical justification provided for each recommended component.
  • Documentation Quality (15%): README clarity, report quality, and screenshot evidence.
